newsitem.title: INDIA: ACC takes over eastern Indian cement firm.
newsitem.headline: ACC takes over eastern Indian cement firm.

text.p: India's largest cement firm Associated Cement Companies (ACC) on Thursday said it took over Damodar Cement and Slag Ltd which runs a cement plant in the eastern state of West Bengal.
The acquisition follows a decision by the Board of Industrial Finance and Reconstruction (BIFR), the Indian authority entrusted with reviving loss-making firms.
"ACC has acquired 13.19 million shares held so far by Cement Corporation of India and the West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation," an ACC statement said.

It said BIFR reduced the paid up value of the existing shares of the company to 4.5 rupees from 10. At a board meeting at Calcutta on September 10, ACC nominees were inducted on the board of Damodar Cement, it said.

"With the taking over of the ownership and management of Damodar Cement from September 1, two rakeloads of cement clinker have been supplied to it from ACC's Kymore works (in central India)," ACC said.

ACC said Damodar Cement plans to revive production before September-end. It has a rated capacity of 270,000 tonnes of portland slag cement per year. Slag is supplied by Indian Iron and Steel Company's facilities at Burnpur, it said.
